global.headline: THE ORDER TO SLOW UKRAINE'S STARSHIELD CAME FROM INSIDE THE WHITE HOUSE, REUTERS REPORTS
summary: Reuters, citing two US officials and a Western official briefed on the matter, reported that the order to throttle Starshield came from inside the White House; none named the official who gave it, but the Pentagon was told SpaceX's service for Ukraine's military had to be slowed. Trump said he had not meddled with it. Zelensky said speeds have still not returned: his partners reported "signals from the White House that they would return these capabilities", but asked whether the previous limits were back, "No. But is it coming back now? Yes." He called the cut a "very dangerous and unpleasant surprise" to the network carrying Ukraine's best defence against jet-powered drones.

Hours earlier Trump called Kyiv's renewed refinery strikes "a disgrace" on Newsmax: "All he's doing is making the world oil price higher." Energy analysts told the BBC that the US-Israeli war on Iran, not Ukraine, is the biggest factor in diesel export volumes.

In Brussels, Zelensky was applauded by all 27 EU heads of government and asked for another €70bn for 2027, putting next year's war cost at €155bn. Von der Leyen agreed "we have a gap of €70bn that has to be covered" but expects other partners to carry part. December's €90bn plan was to cover two-thirds of Kyiv's 2026–27 needs, and the shortfall puts Russia's €210bn frozen in the EU back on the table; Belgium, which holds most of it, remains opposed, and Zelensky floated "a special EU-controlled custodian". Asked whether European leaders had urged him to tone down his criticism of Trump, Zelensky said he heard "only support".
global.geopolitical: The sourcing moves the throttling from suspicion to policy, and locates it in the White House rather than at SpaceX or the Pentagon. With the inspector general already asked by both parties to investigate, the question is no longer whether an ally's air defence was degraded but who ordered it.
global.socioeconomic: Kyiv's 2027 gap is the size of a mid-sized member state's annual budget, and the only pot large enough is Russian money Belgium will not release. Either Europe invents a custodian structure that survives Belgian objection, or Ukraine's defence budget is cut to fit.

global.headline: SHIP ATTACKS NEAR HORMUZ HIT A RECORD AS IRAN DENIES DIRECTING THE HOUTHIS AND BRENT CLOSES ABOVE US$109
summary: BBC Verify's analysis of UK Maritime Trade Operations data counted 12 vessels attacked between 5 and 11 October, the highest weekly total since the war began and up from 10 the week before, with six struck on 11 October alone and four more since. Flows through the strait had recovered to about 15m barrels a day at end-September and were back down to roughly 12.6m by 13 October.

Iran's foreign ministry spokesman Esmaeil Baqaei answered Riyadh's accusation of the previous day: "The Islamic Republic of Iran rejects any claim that Iran has played a role in Yemeni (Houthi) operations. Yemen's armed forces act according to their own interests and assessments." Tehran "does not consider an escalation of tensions to be in the interests of any party", he said, repeating its offer of good offices. Saudi deputy minister for public diplomacy Rayed Krimly had said Iran "encouraged" the escalation and that the Houthis refused a meeting in Oman.

The Saudi-led coalition said it destroyed three drones over the southern region and Riyadh, two cruise missiles over the Red Sea and a ballistic missile over Yanbu, where a major Red Sea oil pipeline terminates. The UN Security Council condemned the attacks "in the strongest terms", citing the 10 and 11 October strikes on King Khalid International Airport, and affirmed the kingdom's right of self-defence. Brent settled at US$109.86, up 3.7% and its highest since 19 May; WTI settled at US$101.41, up 3.5% and its first close above US$100 since 17 September.
global.geopolitical: Tehran's formula — no role in the operations, but ready to mediate them to a close — claims the power to stop the campaign while disowning responsibility for it. Accepting that offer now would concede Riyadh's premise, which is why no mediator has been accepted since 13 October.
global.socioeconomic: With flows down from 15m to 12.6m barrels a day, it is the shipping campaign rather than February's closure now setting the price. Brent above US$109 feeds straight into the fuel and food inflation already visible in September's US prints, and into Singapore's import bill.

global.headline: WASHINGTON'S DEFICIT COMES IN AT US$1.992 TRILLION AS THE AI CREDIT TRADE CRACKS
summary: Treasury's final fiscal 2026 accounts put the deficit at US$1.992 trillion, 12% above last year's US$1.775 trillion and the third-largest on record behind 2020 and 2021, on roughly US$5.4 trillion of receipts against US$7.4 trillion of outlays. Gross interest on the debt was a record US$1.36 trillion, up US$144bn, and net interest passed US$1 trillion — about two-thirds of the US$217bn rise in the shortfall. Gross federal debt is above US$40.3 trillion. Iran war spending and refunds of the US$166bn in tariffs the Supreme Court voided in February account for most of the rest.

The Nasdaq Composite fell 2.1% to 26,140, its worst week since June at about 4.5% down; the S&P 500 lost 1.1% on the day and nearly 2% on the week; the Dow slipped 0.3%. CoreWeave dropped close to 12%, around 24% across the week, with yields on its bonds past 15%, and filings showed its chief executive has sold nearly US$1bn of stock since the IPO.
global.geopolitical: A government borrowing roughly a quarter of what it spends, at record interest, while fighting in the Gulf has less room to fund anyone else. The €70bn Kyiv asked Europe for the same day is that arithmetic seen from the other end.
global.socioeconomic: The AI build-out is now financed at distressed-credit prices — 15% is not a growth-company bond yield — three weeks before a Fed widely expected to tighten into a fuel shock. If those yields hold, the capital spending carrying US growth gets repriced, and the order books with it.

global.headline: DELHI DETAINS THE 'COCKROACH' FOUNDER AGAIN AS PROTESTERS REACH CONNAUGHT PLACE
summary: Police took Cockroach Janta Party founder Abhijeet Dipke into preventive detention as he stepped out of a house in central Delhi, and student activist Neha Bora as she tried to reach Connaught Place; senior officer Sachin Sharma confirmed both. Hundreds of police in riot gear fanned out and civic authorities shut Central Park, but nearly 500 protesters reached about half a dozen spots around it, waving the national flag, with smaller protests in Mumbai, Bengaluru and Patna. Dipke had called the rally for two CJP leaders jailed for five days this week for demonstrating at a banned site.

The demand is the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar over a roll revision that deleted more than 130 million voters. The Election Commission denies favouring any party and says the wrongly deleted can re-enrol; the BJP says its rivals are undermining confidence in a legitimate process.
global.geopolitical: Detaining the movement's two most recognisable figures before a flag-waving rally turns an argument about electoral administration into one about the right to assemble — the ground the opposition's Supreme Court petition already stands on, and a harder one to win in public.
global.socioeconomic: 130 million names is close to a tenth of the population, and the remedy offered is individual re-enrolment. That burden falls hardest on migrant and informal workers, least able to produce documents or give up a day's earnings to do it.

global.headline: AMAZON DEFORESTATION FALLS TO ITS LOWEST ON RECORD, WITH A RUNOFF THAT COULD REVERSE IT ON 25 OCTOBER
summary: Brazil's Prodes satellite series, compiled by the National Institute for Space Research and the most accurate measure available, showed Amazon forest clearance fell 41.8% over the past year to 3,335 sq km — the lowest since measurements began in 1988, and 1,236 sq km below the previous record low. Clearance is down 71.2% since 2022, attributed mainly to stronger enforcement and state investment in environmental agencies. Pará accounted for 33.9% of the total, Mato Grosso 25.5% and Amazonas 15.7%; only Roraima rose, by 0.4%. The neighbouring Cerrado recorded 5,516 sq km, its lowest since 2001.

Jair Bolsonaro's 2019–23 term saw Amazon deforestation rise 59.5%; his son Flávio, who led the first round, has promised to free his father and courts landowning and extractive interests, and former environment minister Marina Silva warns he will finish his father's "perverse project".
global.geopolitical: The number is Brazil's principal asset in climate diplomacy and its argument for sovereignty over the basin rather than international stewardship of it. Whether it survives is settled by the 25 October runoff, which makes the world's largest carbon sink a line item in a vote nobody outside Brazil gets.
global.socioeconomic: Enforcement and agency budgets produced this fall, not commodity prices, so holding it requires recurrent public spending. A government that cuts those budgets gets the 2019–23 trajectory back without passing a law.

singapore.headline: NEA SENDS THE FIRST NOTICES UNDER SINGAPORE'S NEVER-USED HAZE LAW TO SEVEN INDONESIAN COMPANIES
summary: At the first press conference called since the air turned unhealthy in September, Grace Fu said NEA has sent legal notices to seven companies under the Transboundary Haze Pollution Act: "Our investigation so far suggests that some of the haze experienced in Singapore originated from fires on the lands of seven companies in Indonesia." The preventive measure notices require each firm to deploy firefighting personnel to extinguish or stop the spread of fire on land it owns or occupies, to discontinue or not begin burning, and to submit action plans to NEA. Investigations into four companies opened in 2015 are still running. "It is not easy, I will be the first to admit, but we must try," Fu said, "even if it may not be so effective." NEA has not named the seven; Greenpeace's 5 October report named SGX-listed Bumitama Agri and First Resources and privately held First Borneo Plantations as holding land where fires were detected.

Fu warned air quality may reach hazardous levels above 300 PSI, with relief likely only at the inter-monsoon in three to four weeks and the north-east monsoon turning winds away from Sumatra and Kalimantan around early December. Twelve consecutive days of unhealthy readings since 5 October is the longest run since 2015, when it lasted 15 days; central Singapore stood at 226 at 8am on 16 October, and the episode has run close to six weeks since 4 September, as 2015 did. About 10% of eligible Singaporeans have collected N95 masks since distribution began on 14 October, with vending machines at 37 transport hubs and social service offices by Friday.

Desmond Lee said MOE will consider rescheduling O-level papers and closing pre-school to secondary levels for home-based learning if the PSI forecast reaches hazardous, while A-levels proceed because those students are older. Jasmin Lau said MOM has told platform-work employers not to penalise riders who take longer on jobs; about three-quarters of employers inspected had haze measures in place.
singapore.geopolitical: NUS's Jolene Lin said international law is clear that Indonesia may do as it wishes with its resources so long as it causes no harm beyond its borders, which gives Singapore the right to apply its own law — but "the decision to do so has diplomatic implications", and in 2015 drew complaints that the Act infringed Indonesian sovereignty.
singapore.socioeconomic: Norton Rose Fulbright's Wilson Ang said firms within Singapore's jurisdiction have a "direct nexus" exposing them to enforcement, and directors who cannot show they are not contributing risk "legal liability, reputational damage and the inability to secure financing". The pressure falls on listed planters' access to capital here, not on Indonesian enforcement that has produced nothing in eleven years.

singapore.headline: SINGAPORE'S SAUDI TRAVEL ADVISORY REACHES THE UMRAH SEASON
summary: MFA has advised Singaporeans to defer all travel to Saudi Arabia on heightened security risks, and MUIS on 14 October asked those planning Umrah to consider postponing, as missile and drone attacks reach Saudi airports. One family's pilgrimage collapsed hours before check-in on 14 October when their Emirates flight from Dubai was cancelled; booked with OneOasis Travel until 25 October, they were "heartbroken" and now weigh next year. Others proceed while watching: Denise Deanna Chew, travelling 3–13 November with her husband and two sons, said "I believe having faith doesn't mean disregarding safety or taking unnecessary risks," and would reconsider on a stronger advisory or a cancelled flight.
singapore.geopolitical: A defer-all-travel advisory is an unusual instrument to apply to a country Singapore has no quarrel with, and it is the Houthi airport campaign rather than any Saudi policy that produced it. The war now reaches Singaporean Muslims as a question about a religious obligation.
singapore.socioeconomic: Umrah can be performed at any time of year, so deferral is possible in a way the Haj would not be — but deposits, packages and non-refundable fares sit with families and small operators, and an advisory is not a cancellation.

singapore.headline: A STEM-CELL CENTRE BUILT FOR THE ASIAN HEART OPENS IN SINGAPORE
summary: The Centre for Integrative Human Cell Research and Translation (CIPHER) was launched on 16 October by Senior Minister of State for Health Tan Kiat How at the National Heart Centre Singapore's Heart to Heart Gala. It reprograms a 5ml blood sample into induced pluripotent stem cells to grow a patient's own beating heart muscle, drawing on an NHCS library of more than 40 patient-derived models of heart failure, arrhythmogenic disorders and cardiomyopathy. Deputy director Chrishan Ramachandra said Asian patients develop heart disease earlier, present different symptoms and fare worse than Western counterparts, yet the models behind their treatments were built largely on animal models and Western biology: "When we grow a heart muscle cell from a patient's own blood and watch it beat in a dish, carrying that patient's disease, we are looking at something no animal model can replicate." Director Derek Hausenloy said the platforms show "which patients are more likely to be responsive without giving the drug to the patient himself". NHCS also announced a S$2.5 million Tong Ming Chuan Professorship.
singapore.geopolitical: The research asset is the ethnic range of Singapore's own population — Chinese, Malay and Indian, as Hausenloy put it — which lets a small state claim a field whose reference data has been Western, and makes any resulting therapy one the region's regulators can act on rather than adapt.
singapore.socioeconomic: Cardiovascular disease was one in three deaths in Singapore in 2025, about 23 a day. Testing a drug on a patient's own cells before prescribing it targets the waste and harm of trial-and-error prescribing rather than new discovery — the cheaper gain, in a population just past the 21% super-aged threshold.

word.definition: The application of a state's law beyond its own borders, to conduct or persons outside its territory.
word.etymology: From Latin extra, 'outside', and territorium, 'the land around a town', reaching English in the mid-19th century via French extraterritorialité, where it first described diplomats' immunity from the law of the country they were posted to.
word.example: The seven haze notices are an exercise in extraterritoriality: a Singapore statute ordering companies in Indonesia to put out fires on their own land.
